chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Dawud al-Raqqi said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, indeed a man from the companions of Abu al-Khattab forbade me from eating the bukhth and from eating the musarwal pigeon.' He said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'There is no harm in riding the bukhth and drinking its milk and eating the musarwal pigeon.'

key_terms.الْبُخْت: A type of wild duck or waterfowl

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating bukhth and musarwal pigeens according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of consuming specific types of birds, specifically the bukhth (a type of wild duck or goose) and the musarwal pigeon, correcting a prohibition previously reported by a companion. This ruling emphasizes that these animals are halal for consumption, highlighting the Imam's role in refining fiqh based on direct observation and tradition. The hadith underscores the importance of distinguishing between authentic prophetic traditions and the opinions of individual companions in Shia jurisprudence.
